rules.title: FEHA limits on criminal-history screening of rental applicants
rules.requirement: Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must rest on a conviction directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; no use of arrests without conviction, sealed/expunged, or juvenile records
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.coverage_text: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, property management companies and real estate agents.
rules.penalty: Remedies for housing discrimination include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, injunction, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.extraction_note: Source is CRD agency guidance summarizing FEHA, not the statute; no section number or effective/enacted date given. Unclear from text whether the owner-occupied single-boarder exemption applies to criminal-history protections, so set false.

rules.title: FEHA prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in rental screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not refuse to rent or apply different terms based on how a tenant will pay rent, including Section 8 Housing Choice vouchers and other government rental assistance. Refusing to comply with subsidy program requirements or advertising 'No Section 8' is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Source of income (incl. Section 8 vouchers) is a protected characteristic
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).
rules.coverage_text: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, property management companies and real estate agents.
rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but still may not make, print or publish discriminatory statements, notices or advertisements.
rules.penalty: Remedies for housing discrimination include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, injunction, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.extraction_note: Source is CRD agency guidance summarizing FEHA, not the statute; no section number or effective/enacted date given. The owner-occupied exemption is limited to an owner renting to one additional person.
